Options:
 --suite <id-or-name> Eval suite nam
e or ID\n --file <path> Versioned suite file to upload and run (.yaml or .json, or - for stdin)\n --
project <id-or-name> Project name or ID (defaults to the most recently updated project)\n --server <id-or-name
...> Override the suite's saved server selection (HTTP servers only)\n --environment <id-or-name...>
Attached project environment(s) to run. Several values start one PAID RUN each.\n --client <id-or-name...> Atta
ched client(s) to run, so the run is stamped with that client's config. Several values start one PAID RUN each.\n --host <id-or-n
ame...> Deprecated alias for --client. NOT the host-compat catalog id `mcpjam tools --host` takes.\n --all-tar
gets Run EVERY attached environment (or, if none, every attached host) — one PAID RUN per target\n --
iterations <n> Run each case this many times under verdict policy 2 (1-10)\n --repetitions <n>
Legacy spelling of --iterations\n --case <id-or-title...> Run only these cases instead of the wh
ole suite\n --exclude-skills Run the 'without skills' arm: no skills are pinned, and the run is labelled
as excluded\n --refresh-snapshot PERSISTS a new host-config snapshot on the suite, changing every future
run of it. Single-target runs only.\n --notes <text> Free-text note stored on the run\n --min-pass-ra
te <n> Pass threshold for this run (0-100)\n --match-options <json> Tool-call match opti
ons for this run, e.g. '{\"toolCallOrder\":\"exact\"}'\n --idempotency-key <key> Retry key for a lost launch re
sponse; for --file, one is minted and printed when omitted\n --wait Wait for every started run
to reach a terminal status\n --wait-timeout <ms> Maximum time to wait for completion (default 600000; a ru
n held for its judge gets up to 31 more minutes unless this flag is set)\n --reporter <json-summary|junit-xml|html> Render the c
ompleted run report to stdout\n --out <path> Atomically write the completed report selected by --rep
orter (default: json-summary)\n --compose-client <id-or-name> Compose a stack to run instead of naming a saved enviro
nment: the client it runs as. Default is EPHEMERAL (does not attach to the suite).\n --compose-host <id-or-name> De
precated alias for --compose-client\n --compose-computer <id-or-name> Sandbox image to pin on the composed stack\n --c
ompose-model <id...> Model(s) to run on the composed stack. Replaces the client default unless --with-client-def
ault is set.\n --compose-model-selection <json...> A whole saved model selection (source, connection, settings.reasoningEff
ort) as JSON (or @file, or -): one cell for its model, at its effort. Alongside --compose-model. Repeat it to add several selectio
ns for one model (e.g. at low and at high) — each distinct selection is its own cell.\n --with-client-default
Also launch an inherit cell that uses each client's pinned model, alongside --compose-model\n --save-targets
Attach the composed environments to the suite (append, capped at 10). Default is ephemeral.\n --compose-server <id-or-nam
e...> Server(s) to pin on the composed stack. Snapshots them into a server group, so the run keeps testing these servers
even if the host's own server list changes later. Mutually exclusive with --compose-server-group.\n --compose-server-group <id>
Standalone server group to pin on the composed stack\n --compose-host-servers No longer supported
: eval runs take their servers from a server group. Use --compose-server or --compose-server-group.\n --compose-skill <id...>
Project-shared skill IDs to pin on the composed stack\n --compose-secret <id...> Project SECRET I
Ds the composed stack grants to its runs. Without one a composed stack carries no credential — list them with `mcpjam secrets list

atable. --file only, and requires --approval-reason.\n --approval-reason <text> Why the approximations named by
